questions.question_text:
A scientist found that the time taken, $M$ minutes, to carry out an experiment can be modelled by a normal random variable with mean 155 minutes and standard deviation 3.5 minutes.

Find
(a) $\mathrm{P}(M>160)$,
(3)
(b) $\mathrm{P}(150 \leqslant M \leqslant 157)$,
(4)
(c) the value of $m$, to 1 decimal place, such that $\mathrm{P}(M \leqslant m) = 0.30$.
(4)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $M \sim \mathrm{N}(155, 3.5^2)$
$\mathrm{P}(M>160) = \mathrm{P}\left(z > \frac{160-155}{3.5}\right)$ standardising $\pm(160-155), \sigma, \sigma^2, \sqrt{\sigma}$ M1
$= \mathrm{P}(z>1.43)$ A1
$= 0.0764$ A1
(3)
(b) $\mathrm{P}(150 \leqslant M \leqslant 157) = \mathrm{P}(-1.43 \leqslant z \leqslant 0.57)$ awrt $-1.43$, $0.57$ B1 B1
$= 0.7157 - (1-0.9236)$ $p>0.5$ M1
$= 0.6393$ $0.6393 - 0.6400$ 4dp A1
(4)
Special case: answer only B0 B0 M1 A1
(c) $\mathrm{P}(M \leqslant m) = 0.3 \Rightarrow \frac{m-155}{3.5} = -0.5244$ $-0.5244$ B1
att stand $=$ $z$ value for A1 may use awrt to $-0.52$ M1 A1
$m = 153.2$ cao A1
(4)

questions.stem:
In a school there are 148 students in Years 12 and 13 studying Science, Humanities or Arts subjects. Of these students, 89 wear glasses and the others do not. There are 30 Science students of whom 18 wear glasses. The corresponding figures for the Humanities students are 68 and 44 respectively.

A student is chosen at random.

Find the probability that this student

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) [table: Science: Glasses 18, No Glasses 12, Totals 30; Arts: Glasses 27, No Glasses 23, Totals 50; Humanities: Glasses 44, No Glasses 24, Totals 68; Totals: Glasses 89, No Glasses 59, Totals 148] 50 may be seen in (a), 23 may be seen in (b) B1 B1
$\mathrm{P}(\text{Arts}) = \frac{50}{148} = \frac{25}{74} = 0.338$ a number$/148$ M1 A1
(4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) does not wear glasses, given that the student is studying Arts subjects.
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Amongst the Science students, 80% are right-handed. Corresponding percentages for Humanities and Arts students are 75% and 70% respectively.

A student is again chosen at random.

(c) Find the probability that this student is right-handed.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathrm{P}(\text{Right Handed}) = \left(\frac{30}{148} \times 0.8\right) + \left(\frac{50}{148} \times 0.7\right) + \left(\frac{68}{148} \times 0.75\right)$ attempt add three prob M1 A1$\surd$ on their (a)
$= \frac{55}{74} = 0.743$ awrt 0.743 A1
(3)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Given that this student is right-handed, find the probability that the student is studying Science subjects.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\mathrm{P}(\text{Science} / \text{Right handed}) = \frac{\frac{30}{148} \times 0.8}{(c)} = \frac{12}{55} = 0.218$ $\surd$ on their (c) M1 A1$\surd$ A1
(3)
